title: Dispatch CUS 1: Census Lists Families on Streets Alderwick Never Built
summary: The new returns give house numbers, occupations, and children for two absent streets.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Twenty-three households appear in the preliminary municipal census under the headings Fenwick Lane and Vesper Row. Neither street exists. The lanes were proposed in an 1887 improvement scheme that the council rejected before a stone was laid.

Registrar Agnes Morrow noticed the entries while checking the total for the north ward. They are complete to the last column: residents’ ages, trades, and the number of rooms in each house. Several names are unknown to present rate books. Others belong to people already counted elsewhere in Alderwick.

One duplicate is Samuel Keene, a bookbinder living above his shop on North Loom Street. The second entry calls him deceased and lists his wife Ada as head of a household on Vesper Row. Mrs. Keene died nine years ago. Mr. Keene asks that both entries be preserved until someone can tell him who supplied them.

Surveyor Tomas Reed placed the listed addresses against the 1887 drawing. Fenwick Lane crosses three existing courtyards. Vesper Row passes through the north end of North Loom Street, including the site of Mr. Keene’s shop. The numbered plots fit the rejected drawing precisely.

Miss Morrow has locked the census sheets away and requested assistance from the Eidetical Institute. The entries bear the signatures of enumerators employed this year, but those workers say they have never walked either street. One signature is beside a door number that would lie inside the registrar’s own office.
